study type: Retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis at birth
cohort: A multinational cohort of 132,727 (for birth weight) and 65,406 (for head circumference) preterm neonates born between 22 and 29 weeks gestation to mothers without hypertension or diabetes and without major congenital anomalies.
finding: The study generated updated sex-specific birth weight and head circumference percentiles for 22-29 week preterm neonates, observing general comparability between countries but finding that caesarean births had higher 10th percentile birth weights than vaginal births after 26 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: Caesarean births had birth weights similar to vaginal births until 26 weeks, after which the 10th percentile for birth weight diverged (caesarean births approximately 239g heavier at 29 weeks), and vaginal births' birth weights closely matched intrauterine estimated fetal weights, while no differences in head circumference were observed by mode of birth.
birth_weight: Varied, for neonates between 22-29 weeks gestation, excluding data truncated by 1500g cut-offs.
